detailed_rationale:
Clean Science & Technology is one of the higher-quality specialty-chemical franchises in our coverage on paper -- debt-free (just Rs 2 Cr borrowings against Rs 957 Cr FY26 sales), with global leadership positions in niche products like MEHQ, BHA, Ascorbyl Palmitate and Guaiacol across three segments (Performance Chemicals 72% of revenue, Pharma & Agro Intermediates 19%, FMCG Chemicals 9%). FY26 delivered Rs 957 Cr sales and Rs 230 Cr net profit at a 37% operating margin -- margins any specialty chemical peer would envy -- but the trend within the year is the more important signal: margins ran 41% in Q1 FY26 before compressing to 33-36% in Q2-Q3 and partially recovering to 36% by Q4, and the company's own data shows profit growth down roughly 13% year-to-date, consistent with real pricing/competitive pressure (global oversupply in some of these performance-chemical categories has been a broader Indian specialty-chem theme over the past two years).

Promoter holding has fallen sharply, from 78.5% (Mar 2022) to 51.3% (Mar 2026) -- a meaningful ~27-point reduction that is large enough to flag even though it looks consistent with a gradual, long-running secondary sell-down rather than a sudden exit, and the business itself shows no balance-sheet stress alongside it (still essentially debt-free).

At a PE of roughly 35-36x, the valuation is not demanding relative to the extraordinary margin profile (33%+ OPM, ROE 28%, ROCE 38.5%), but it does assume the recent growth softness is a pause rather than a structural share-loss story; the honest read is that we cannot yet distinguish between the two from the data available.
recommendation_rationale: Hold, matching the quant score -- the underlying franchise quality (debt-free, industry-leading margins, strong ROE/ROCE) is genuinely excellent and argues against any Sell bias, but recent growth deceleration and margin compression versus a year ago mean we are not inclined to describe this as anything stronger than Hold until growth reaccelerates.
summary: Clean Science & Technology is a debt-free, high-margin specialty chemicals maker with global leadership positions in several niche products. FY26 margins remain strong (37% operating margin) but growth has slowed and margins compressed somewhat during the year versus year-ago levels, likely reflecting industry-wide pricing pressure. We rate it a Hold: an excellent-quality balance sheet and margin profile, but growth needs to reaccelerate to justify paying up further.
positive_para: This is a genuinely high-quality franchise: essentially debt-free, 28% ROE, 38.5% ROCE, and operating margins in the 33-41% range that few Indian chemical companies can match, built on defensible global-leadership positions in several niche molecules. There is real balance-sheet and margin cushion here even through a soft patch.
negative_para: Growth has clearly slowed -- profit is down roughly 13% year-to-date per the company's own reported trend, and quarterly margins compressed from 41% to the low-to-mid 30s before a partial recovery, most plausibly reflecting competitive/pricing pressure in some performance-chemical categories. Promoter holding has also fallen sharply (down ~27 points over three years), a scale of dilution large enough to want an explanation for, even without evidence of anything beyond a gradual planned sell-down.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~35-36x earnings, the market is paying a premium multiple justified by best-in-class margins and returns, but that premium assumes the recent growth slowdown is temporary. If competitive/pricing pressure in performance chemicals persists, a business with high margins but decelerating growth typically de-rates even without any balance-sheet problem -- the quality is real, but the price is not obviously cheap against a slower growth path.
